result.topic_en: Ramanujan defines the infinite product φ(α,β) = ∏{1+((α+β)/(n+α))^3} and evaluates φ(α,β)φ(β,α) in terms of Gamma functions and hyperbolic/trigonometric functions, concluding that the product can be expressed in finite terms when α−β is an integer.
result.transcription:
Add Ms a 94$^{18(56)}$ (56) (1)

1. Let
$\phi(\alpha,\beta) = \left\{1+\left(\frac{\alpha+\beta}{1+\alpha}\right)^3\right\}\left\{1+\left(\frac{\alpha+\beta}{2+\alpha}\right)^3\right\}\left\{1+\left(\frac{\alpha+\beta}{3+\alpha}\right)^3\right\}\cdots\cdots$
It can easily be shown that
(1) $\left\{1+\left(\frac{\alpha+\beta}{n+\alpha}\right)^3\right\}\left\{1+\left(\frac{\alpha+\beta}{n+\beta}\right)^3\right\} = \frac{\left(1+\frac{\alpha+2\beta}{n}\right)\left(1+\frac{2\alpha+\beta}{n}\right)}{\left(1+\frac{\alpha}{n}\right)^3\left(1+\frac{\beta}{n}\right)^3}\times$
$\left\{1-\left(\frac{(\alpha-\beta)+i(\alpha+\beta)\sqrt{3}}{2n}\right)^2\right\}\left\{1-\left(\frac{(\alpha-\beta)-i(\alpha+\beta)\sqrt{3}}{2n}\right)^2\right\}$;
(2) $\prod_{n=1}^{n=\infty}\frac{\left(1+\frac{\alpha+2\beta}{n}\right)\left(1+\frac{2\alpha+\beta}{n}\right)}{\left(1+\frac{\alpha}{n}\right)^3\left(1+\frac{\beta}{n}\right)^3} = \frac{\{\Gamma(1+\alpha)\Gamma(1+\beta)\}^3}{\Gamma(1+\alpha+2\beta)\Gamma(1+\beta+2\alpha)}$;
(3) $\prod_{n=1}^{n=\infty}\left\{1-\left(\frac{(\alpha-\beta)+i(\alpha+\beta)\sqrt{3}}{2n}\right)^2\right\}\left\{1-\left(\frac{(\alpha-\beta)-i(\alpha+\beta)\sqrt{3}}{2n}\right)^2\right\}$
$= \frac{\cosh\pi(\alpha+\beta)\sqrt{3}-\cos\pi(\alpha-\beta)}{2\pi^2(\alpha^2+\alpha\beta+\beta^2)}$.
It follows from (1), (2) and (3) that
(4) $\phi(\alpha,\beta)\phi(\beta,\alpha) = \frac{\{\Gamma(1+\alpha)\Gamma(1+\beta)\}^3}{\Gamma(1+\alpha+2\beta)\Gamma(1+\beta+2\alpha)}\cdot\frac{\cosh\pi(\alpha+\beta)\sqrt{3}-\cos\pi(\alpha-\beta)}{2\pi^2(\alpha^2+\alpha\beta+\beta^2)}$
But $\phi(\alpha,\beta)/\phi(\beta,\alpha)$ can be expressed in finite terms if $\alpha-\beta$ be any integer. It follows from (4) that, if $\alpha-\beta$ be any integer, then $\phi(\alpha,\beta)$ can be expressed in finite terms. That is to say
(5) $\left\{1+\left(\frac{x}{n+1}\right)^3\right\}\left\{1+\left(\frac{x}{n+2}\right)^3\right\}\left\{1+\left(\frac{x}{n+3}\right)^3\right\}\cdots\cdots$
can be expressed in finite terms, if $x-2n$ be any integer.
